summary: Seat-pin reconciliation: reclaim leaked catalog pins from expired holds
description:
Deferred from TKT-80 (ADR-031). Hold-then-pin unpins on explicit release and best-effort on the next pool mutation's sweep, but a seated pool that is never touched again after an on-sale can leak catalog `seat_map_pins` rows from TTL-expired holds. A leaked pin fails SAFE — it blocks a now-safe map edit (409), never orphans or oversells — but it degrades an organizer's ability to edit a published map over time.

**Scope:** a one-shot `reconcile-pins` subcommand (inventory or catalog binary) that reconciles `seat_map_pins` (pinned_by='hold:*') against live inventory `claim_seats` and unpins the dead ones. Must NOT have inventory read the catalog DB (ADR-010) — reconcile over the existing internal HTTP contract, or as a catalog-side job fed the live hold set. The manually-callable internal batch-unpin endpoint (shipped in TKT-80) is the interim operator remedy.

**COS:** given N expired-hold pins with no live claim, the subcommand removes exactly those and leaves confirmed-sale and live-hold pins intact; idempotent; honest-writer only (ADR-021).

objective.note: TTL-expired seat holds leave catalog seat_map_pins rows behind on a seated pool that is never mutated again; they fail safe but block a now-safe published-map edit (409) forever. ADR-031 deferred the cleanup automation here.

scope.note: IN: one-shot operator subcommand that reconciles hold:* pins against live inventory claim_seats and unpins the dead ones; idempotent; runs over the existing internal HTTP contract (a new internal read may be added). OUT: background worker/outbox/scheduler (ADR-031 §4 explicitly refuses one), sale:* pins, per-version membership checks (ADR-031 open question), any change to the hold/pin write path.

uncertainties.note: Two named and resolvable at Planning: (1) which binary hosts the subcommand — inventory owns hold liveness, catalog owns the pin table, and neither may read the other's DB (ADR-010/002), so one new internal endpoint is needed either way; (2) the disposition of a hold:<id> pin whose claim inventory has never seen — must fail safe (leave + report), not unpin.

dependencies.note: blocked-by TKT-80 (Done, shipped ADR-031 + the batch pin/unpin endpoint this reuses). No open blockers.

approach.note: Copy the established one-shot subcommand shape (services/inventory/cmd/inventory/reprocess.go: injectable core struct + thin env/DB/HTTP wiring outer func, ADR-022 registry in main.go subcommands()). Unpins go through the existing family-advisory-locked store path (POST /internal/seat-maps/{id}/unpins), never a raw DELETE (ADR-029).

first_slice.note: The whole ticket is one slice: subcommand + whatever internal read it needs + unit test on the reconciler core + a store/smoke test proving the selective-unpin behaviour. Well under the ~400-line target.

success.note: COS on the ticket description: given N expired-hold pins with no live claim, exactly those are removed; confirmed-sale and live-hold pins survive; idempotent (a second run is a no-op); honest-writer only (ADR-021 — the reconciler guards our own bugs, not an adversary with DB write access).

context_memo.note: Baked at claim time (context.governingAdrs below), re-resolved against docs/adr/ at HEAD 2520164 — all eight cited ADRs verified to exist.

governingAdrs.why: The decision this ticket completes: hold-then-pin, best-effort unpin on the next pool mutation, and an EXPLICIT refusal of a background worker/outbox (§4). So the deliverable is a one-shot operator command, not a sweeper — and §Consequences already names the interim remedy (the manually-callable batch-unpin endpoint) this automates.

Inventory is the sole write-side correctness boundary and NEVER reads or writes the catalog database. The reconciler must cross the service line over internal HTTP, not SQL — this is what makes the naive 'join pins against claim_seats' implementation illegal here.
One database per service; the pin table lives in catalog, claim_seats in inventory. Same constraint from the other direction: a catalog-hosted job may not read inventory's DB either.

The pin contract: pins key on (map_family_id, seat_identity, pinned_by) and every pin/unpin/edit serializes on a FAMILY-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock, not a row lock. Any unpin the reconciler performs must go through that locked store path (UnpinSeats), never a bare DELETE, or it races a concurrent edit.

Out-of-band one-shot subcommands are the established placement for operator jobs (each binary's own subcommand, run as a Compose one-shot). reconcile-pins joins the same registry as migrate / reprocess-quarantine / access verify-lifecycle; the server path never runs it.

Service-to-service routes are HAND-MOUNTED internal paths outside the public OpenAPI contract (the existing /internal/seat-maps/{id}/pins|unpins are exactly this). Any new internal read this ticket adds follows that convention and is NOT declared in the spec — the response validator skips undeclared paths (ADR-028).

A scoped read is only scoped if an index backs the filter, and proving it takes two assertions (result scoped AND scan scoped). If the reconciler adds a pins-by-family read, seat_map_pins_by_family already backs it — say so rather than adding an index.

Name the adversary before claiming a guarantee. This reconciler is honest-writer consistency only: state inside a database cannot constrain a writer with access to that database. The COS says 'honest-writer only' for exactly this reason — do not let the plan or the docs imply tamper-evidence.

reference.summary: The one-shot subcommand shape to copy: injectable core struct (quarantineReprocessor) + thin outer func owning env/DB/NATS, registered in main.go subcommands(); unit-tested with fakes, no DB
Existing internal batch pin/unpin endpoints + shared decodeBatchPin (the interim operator remedy this automates)
Catalog's family-locked pin store path — PinSeat/UnpinSeat/PinSeats/UnpinSeats
Inventory's hold-side pin coordinates: PinRef, SeatHold.ExpiredPins, seatsAboutToExpire, SeatPinRef
Inventory's HTTP client to the catalog pin contract (CatalogResolver.PinSeats/UnpinSeats/batchPin)
